mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) at t-1mo predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced discount rates for equity valuation.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between FEDFUNDS (t-1mo) and 20-day forward returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in unemployment rate exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises by more than 0.2pp in a month, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% in the prior month signals robust aggregate demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both grow > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: In instances where both HOUST and RSAFS grow > 0.5% in the prior month, the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During the post-recession recovery phase, rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals strengthening supply conditions and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: During the post-recession recovery phase, INDPRO growth is not associated with positive 20-day forward returns (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A higher quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) at t-6mo predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to strong economic momentum.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between GDPC1 (t-6mo) and 5-day forward returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI reading above 2.5% signals elevated inflation, prompting monetary tightening expectations that depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.2 percentage points in the prior month signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS grows > 0.5% and UNRATE falls > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: When PAYEMS grows > 0.5% and UNRATE falls > 0.2pp in a month, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals reduced liquidity and higher discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: During monetary tightening cycles, FEDFUNDS rises but the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
